cards.text: Jonah son of Amittai got a job from the LORD: go to the great city of Nineveh. Instead he bought a ticket the OTHER way, a storm hit his ship, and the sailors threw him overboard. Now he's in the sea, and the sea just went calm, which is the most awkward kind of quiet there is.

cards.question: Jonah's been thrown into the sea, but the LORD already has a plan. What has the LORD appointed?

cards.text: And that great fish swallows Jonah. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even I'm looking at this going, "Okay, Jonah. YOU win."

cards.question: How long is Jonah in the belly of the fish?
Jonah is stuck inside the fish. What does he do from in there?

answers.text: He prays to the LORD his God
He falls into a deep sleep
He cries out to the sailors

cards.question: Jonah's prayer looks back on his distress. He says that when he called for help from the belly of Sheol, the LORD heard his voice.

cards.text: Then Jonah takes us under with him: the deep, the heart of the seas, the current swirling, the waves sweeping right over him. That's not a swim, friend, that's a SPIN CYCLE.

cards.question: In his prayer, who does Jonah say cast him into the deep?

cards.text: Not the sailors, the LORD. Then Jonah tells what he said in that moment: "I have been banished from Your sight"

cards.question: Jonah says he has been banished from God's sight. What does he say he will do next?

answers.text: Look once more toward God's holy temple
Never look toward God's holy temple again
Lift his hands toward God's holy mountain

cards.text: Jonah keeps going: the waters engulf him, and the seaweed wraps around his head. I wear a tall chef's hat every single day, and friend, I have NEVER had a hat day that bad.
He sinks all the way down to the roots of the mountains. He says the earth beneath him barred him in forever.

cards.question: At the very bottom, Jonah says the LORD left his life down in the pit.
As his life was fading away, Jonah ___ the LORD.
Near the end of his prayer, Jonah talks about people who cling to worthless idols. He says they hold on to God's loving devotion.

cards.text: But Jonah sets himself apart from them. He says he'll come to the LORD with the voice of thanksgiving.

cards.question: Jonah says he will ___ to the LORD and fulfill what he has ___.
Jonah ends his prayer by saying that ___ is from the LORD.
Jonah's prayer is done, and the LORD commands the fish. What does the fish do with Jonah?

answers.text: Spits him onto a passing ship
Carries him back out to sea

cards.text: The LORD gives the command, and the fish does exactly what it's told. Friend, I can't even get my own oven timer to listen to me. And trust me, this story is far from done.

findings.problem: The question asks which thing the LORD appointed. The wrong answer "A passing ship" is a generic idea, not a real detail from the Bible. "A strong east wind" works because God appoints a scorching east wind in Jonah 4:8. Replace the ship with another thing the Bible says God appointed or sent, like the plant (Jonah 4:6) or the worm (Jonah 4:7).

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card prepares the baker for the answer "The LORD." Card 1 told the baker that the sailors threw Jonah overboard, and card 7 describes the deep and the waves without hinting at who sent him there. A thoughtful baker would reason their way to "The sailors," so the setup leads toward the wrong answer. Card 7 needs context showing that Jonah's prayer speaks to God about what God did, or the question should change.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: "Not the sailors, the LORD." can read as saying the sailors didn't throw Jonah into the sea, but Jonah 1:15 says they did. The card should keep it as Jonah's own words, for example: Jonah says it was the LORD who cast him in (Jonah 2:3).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Card 9 quotes the first half of Jonah 2:4, and this card asks the baker to finish the same line ("yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple"). The answers come down to wording: "holy temple" or "holy mountain," and "look" or "lift his hands." The baker has to guess the words instead of reasoning about meaning. Ask about the turn in meaning instead, for example whether Jonah gives up or still turns toward God.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The second half of Jonah 2:7, "My prayer went up to You, to Your holy temple," is never told or asked. It is the answer to Jonah 2:4, where Jonah said he felt banished but would look toward the temple once more, and his prayer reaches that very temple. This is the turning point of the prayer, and the baker leaves without it. A story card after card 14 could carry it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 16, right before this card, says Jonah will come to the LORD "with the voice of thanksgiving." That rules out the wrong answer "complain" for the first blank.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "fulfill what he has forgotten" doesn't make sense, so it isn't a believable choice for the second blank. That leaves the baker only "vowed" and "dreamed" to weigh. Replace "forgotten" with a word that fits the sentence believably.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the fish obeys, the oven timer joke, and the story-isn't-over line. Cut it to two, for example by dropping the restatement of Jonah 2:10, which card 19 already covered.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
